statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let P be the set of all integers p for which there exist indices i, j, k with 0 <= i < j < k < len(nums), p = nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k], and the three strict triangle inequalities nums[i] + nums[j] > nums[k], nums[i] + nums[k] > nums[j], and nums[j] + nums[k] > nums[i] hold. If P is nonempty, r is the maximum element of P. If P is empty, r = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 10000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail by overflow, panic, or out-of-bounds access.

statement: For any slice nums' such that len(nums') = len(nums) and nums' is a permutation of nums (the same multiset of entries, possibly in a different order), if largest_perimeter(nums) returns r and largest_perimeter(nums') returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 10000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let c be a positive integer, and let nums' be a slice with len(nums') = len(nums), nums'[i] = c * nums[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), and 1 <= nums'[i] <= 1000000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums'). If largest_perimeter(nums) returns r and largest_perimeter(nums') returns r', then r' = c * r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 10000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: If there exist indices i, j, k with 0 <= i < j < k < len(nums) such that for every index h with 0 <= h < len(nums) and h not in {i, j, k}, nums[h] <= min(nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]), and nums[i] + nums[j] > nums[k], nums[i] + nums[k] > nums[j], and nums[j] + nums[k] > nums[i], then whenever the function returns a result r, r = nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 10000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let b be the entries of nums sorted in nondecreasing order. Let Q be the set of all integers q for which there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-2, q = b[i] + b[i+1] + b[i+2], and b[i] + b[i+1] > b[i+2]. Whenever the function returns a result r, if Q is nonempty then r is the maximum element of Q; if Q is empty then r = 0.
